description:
Close the last evidence gap: the six served signs that carried NO verification record — IN11.1, IN11.2, IN11.3, IN11.4, IN19, W346.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it was worse than the handover recorded. docs/handover-2026-08-04.md item (d) described these as 'approved on both gates with an empty verification field'. True, but it understated it: `content` was `{}` on all six. They were review_status='approved', asset_status='approved', sa_relevant=true — i.e. fully served — with no lesson text at all in either locale. A learner opening /en/learn/road-signs/IN11.1 got artwork, a name, and five empty sections. That is a live content defect, not just a missing audit column.

WHY THE CHART CHECK HAD FAILED. Their chart_match scores explain the empty verification: IN11.1 matched at 0.333 against the chart string 'to IN11.5*', and IN11.2/.3/.4 matched at 0.0 with a null name. None of that is a real naming error — the chart lists the family as the RANGE 'IN11.1 to IN11.5*' (p.2), so the extractor grabbed the tail of a range label and had nothing per-member to match against. John confirmed independently from resources/charts/RTSigns_charts.pdf: the chart's own VARIABLE MESSAGE SIGNS list uses the codes directly — 'VM1 Sliding sign (W333 plus IN11.1)', 'VM6 TW333 plus IN11.1', 'VM8 TR201 plus TW339 plus IN11.4'. The codes are real and ours. IN19 and W346 had already matched at score 1.0 with exact names; they were simply never given content.

WHAT WAS DONE. Every name was checked against the primary sources and every artwork rendered and inspected. SADC RTSM Vol 1 §5.2.5(3) enumerates the six supplementary-plate sub-types verbatim — '(a) an advisory speed numbered IN11.1; (b) a distance "for" numbered IN11.2; (c) a distance "to" numbered IN11.3; (d) a text message numbered IN11.4' — which matches our four names exactly, in order. The rendered artwork matches the same source's own worked examples ('IN11.1 (80 km/h)', 'TIN11.2 (For 2 km)'): ours read '80 km/h', 'For 12km', '200 m', '( TEXT )'. W346's colours match Vol 1 §3.4.37's colour block field-for-field (Triangle: Red retroreflective / Symbol: Yellow flashing light / Background: White retroreflective) — ours is a red triangle with a yellow disc on white.

CONTENT IS AI-DRAFTED AND NOT SELF-CERTIFIED (constraint 9). Every verification block below carries humanSignOff: false. The naming and artwork findings rest on quoted primary text and are strong; the learner prose is a first draft and still needs a human read. THESE SIX SHOULD GO INTO THE NEXT LOUWRENS BATCH — they are now reviewable, which they were not before, because there was nothing to review.

PROSE FOLLOWS CONSTRAINT 10: teaches the driver, no regulation numbers in learner-facing text (those live in verification.verifiedAgainst), and leads with the confusion each sign turns on — for IN11.2/IN11.3 that is the 'for' vs 'to' pair, which is the whole reason the two exist as separate codes.

Afrikaans is a first-pass draft consistent with the rest of the project's AF content, pending native review.

Idempotent: every write is a targeted PATCH to a known value, so reruns are no-ops.

plainEnglish.en: The safe speed for whatever the sign above it is warning about. It is advice, not a new speed limit — but it is the speed that bend or dip can actually be taken at.
plainEnglish.af: Die veilige spoed vir waarteen die teken bo dit waarsku. Dit is raad, nie 'n nuwe spoedgrens nie — maar dit is die spoed waarteen daardie draai of duik werklik gery kan word.

formalMeaning.en: A supplementary plate giving an advisory speed. It hangs directly under a main sign and applies only to the hazard that sign is about.
formalMeaning.af: 'n Aanvullende plaat wat 'n aanbevole spoed gee. Dit hang reg onder 'n hoofteken en geld net vir die gevaar waaroor daardie teken gaan.

behaviour.en: Be down to the speed shown before you reach the hazard, not while you are in it. Brake on the straight, not in the bend.
behaviour.af: Wees reeds teen die aangeduide spoed voordat jy die gevaar bereik, nie terwyl jy daarin is nie. Rem op die reguit stuk, nie in die draai nie.

commonMistake.en: Reading it as the speed limit. Limits are numbers in a red circle; this is a plain plate under another sign, and the legal limit for the road has not changed.
commonMistake.af: Om dit as die spoedgrens te lees. Grense is syfers in 'n rooi sirkel; dit is 'n gewone plaat onder 'n ander teken, en die wetlike grens vir die pad het nie verander nie.

testHint.en: Check where the number sits. In a red circle it is a limit you can be fined for; on a plate under another sign it is advice.
testHint.af: Kyk waar die syfer sit. In 'n rooi sirkel is dit 'n grens waarvoor jy beboet kan word; op 'n plaat onder 'n ander teken is dit raad.

memoryTrick.en: Red circle rules. Plain plate advises.
memoryTrick.af: Rooi sirkel beveel. Gewone plaat raai aan.

The chart uses the code directly elsewhere on the same sheet: 'VM1 Sliding sign (W333 plus IN11.1)' and 'VM6 TW333 plus IN11.1'. SADC RTSM Vol 1 §5.2.5(3)(a) names it verbatim: 'an advisory speed numbered IN11.1'. plainEnglish.en: Tells you how far the warning above it keeps applying. "For 12 km" means the whole stretch, not one spot — stay ready that entire distance.
plainEnglish.af: Sê vir jou hóé ver die waarskuwing bo dit bly geld. "For 12 km" beteken die hele stuk, nie een plek nie — bly daardie hele afstand gereed.

formalMeaning.en: A supplementary plate showing the distance over which the condition on the sign above it continues.
formalMeaning.af: 'n Aanvullende plaat wat die afstand aandui waaroor die toestand op die teken bo dit voortduur.

behaviour.en: Treat the whole distance as the hazard. Do not relax after the first bend or the first rough patch — the sign told you it lasts.
behaviour.af: Hanteer die hele afstand as die gevaar. Moenie ná die eerste draai of eerste growwe stuk ontspan nie — die teken het gesê dit hou aan.

commonMistake.en: Confusing it with the "to" plate. "For" is how long it lasts; "to" is how far off it starts. One says when to stop worrying, the other when to start.
commonMistake.af: Om dit met die "to"-plaat te verwar. "For" is hoe lank dit duur; "to" is hoe ver dit begin. Die een sê wanneer om op te hou bekommer, die ander wanneer om te begin.

testHint.en: Read the word, not just the number. "For" with a distance means duration; a bare distance means how far ahead.
testHint.af: Lees die woord, nie net die syfer nie. "For" met 'n afstand beteken duur; 'n kaal afstand beteken hoe ver vorentoe.

memoryTrick.en: "For" = for how long. It starts now.
memoryTrick.af: "For" = vir hoe lank. Dit begin nou.

plainEnglish.en: Tells you how far ahead the thing on the sign above it starts. "200 m" means you still have 200 m of normal road before it matters.
plainEnglish.af: Sê vir jou hoe ver vorentoe die ding op die teken bo dit begin. "200 m" beteken jy het nog 200 m gewone pad voordat dit saak maak.

formalMeaning.en: A supplementary plate showing the distance from the sign to the hazard or condition it is about.
formalMeaning.af: 'n Aanvullende plaat wat die afstand vanaf die teken tot by die gevaar of toestand aandui waaroor dit gaan.

behaviour.en: Use the distance to get ready — mirrors, speed, gear — so you arrive at the hazard already sorted instead of reacting at it.
behaviour.af: Gebruik die afstand om reg te maak — spieëls, spoed, rat — sodat jy reeds reg by die gevaar aankom eerder as om daar te reageer.

commonMistake.en: Confusing it with the "for" plate and braking on the spot. Nothing changes where you are standing; the distance is how far off it still is.
commonMistake.af: Om dit met die "for"-plaat te verwar en dadelik te rem. Niks verander waar jy nou is nie; die afstand is hoe ver dit nog is.

testHint.en: A bare distance with no "For" in front of it means how far ahead. Put "For" in front and it becomes how long it lasts.
testHint.af: 'n Kaal afstand sonder "For" daarvoor beteken hoe ver vorentoe. Sit "For" daarvoor en dit word hoe lank dit duur.

memoryTrick.en: "To" = how far to go before it starts.
memoryTrick.af: "To" = hoe ver om te gaan voor dit begin.

Vol 1 §3.6.1(2)(c) expands the function as 'distance to the hazard and distance countdown to the hazard (IN11.3)'. plainEnglish.en: A plate with words on it, used when no symbol says the thing that needs saying. Whatever it reads applies to the sign directly above it.
plainEnglish.af: 'n Plaat met woorde daarop, gebruik wanneer geen simbool sê wat gesê moet word nie. Wat ook al daarop staan, geld vir die teken reg bo dit.

formalMeaning.en: A supplementary plate carrying a short text message that qualifies the sign above it.
formalMeaning.af: 'n Aanvullende plaat met 'n kort teksboodskap wat die teken bo dit kwalifiseer.

behaviour.en: Read it and apply it to the sign above. It exists because a symbol could not carry the message, so the words are the whole point.
behaviour.af: Lees dit en pas dit toe op die teken bo dit. Dit bestaan omdat 'n simbool nie die boodskap kon dra nie, so die woorde is die hele punt.

commonMistake.en: Treating the words as a sign in their own right. The plate never stands alone — it only narrows or explains whatever is mounted above it.
commonMistake.af: Om die woorde as 'n teken op sy eie te behandel. Die plaat staan nooit alleen nie — dit verfyn of verduidelik net wat bo dit gemonteer is.

testHint.en: It may be drawn blank or as "(TEXT)". The question is about what a text plate does, not what any one of them happens to say.
testHint.af: Dit kan leeg of as "(TEXT)" geteken word. Die vraag gaan oor wat 'n teksplaat doen, nie oor wat een spesifieke een sê nie.

memoryTrick.en: Words on a plate belong to the sign above them.
memoryTrick.af: Woorde op 'n plaat behoort aan die teken bo hulle.

plainEnglish.en: Marks a transport interchange nearby — a place to swap between car, taxi, bus and train. It is information for getting around, not an instruction to you.
plainEnglish.af: Dui 'n vervoerruilpunt naby aan — 'n plek om tussen motor, taxi, bus en trein oor te klim. Dit is inligting oor rondkom, nie 'n opdrag aan jou nie.

formalMeaning.en: Indicates a transport interchange or terminal close by, at which road users may change from one mode of transport to another.
formalMeaning.af: Dui aan dat daar 'n vervoerruilpunt of terminaal naby is waar padgebruikers van een vervoerwyse na 'n ander kan oorskakel.

behaviour.en: Nothing is demanded of you as a driver. Expect people on foot and buses or taxis pulling over near it, and do not block the stopping area.
behaviour.af: Niks word van jou as bestuurder geëis nie. Verwag mense te voet en busse of taxi's wat naby stilhou, en moenie die stilhouplek versper nie.

commonMistake.en: Reading it as a parking sign or a taxi-rank instruction. It points to where the modes meet; it gives you no right to stop there yourself.
commonMistake.af: Om dit as 'n parkeerteken of taxi-staanplek-opdrag te lees. Dit wys waar die vervoerwyses ontmoet; dit gee jou geen reg om self daar stil te hou nie.

testHint.en: Green is a guidance colour: it tells you what is around, not what you must do. Nothing on this sign can be disobeyed.
testHint.af: Groen is 'n leidingkleur: dit sê wat rondom is, nie wat jy moet doen nie. Niks op hierdie teken kan oortree word nie.

memoryTrick.en: Arrows pointing in from every mode: change here.
memoryTrick.af: Pyle wat van elke vervoerwyse inwys: klim hier oor.

verification.reason: Chart match was already exact — code 'IN19', name 'Modal transfer', p.2, score 1.0, and the chart's own index reads 'IN19 Modal transfer sign'. The gap was content, not identity. SADC RTSM Vol 1 §5.2.11(1): 'MODAL TRANSFER signs IN17, IN18 and IN19 may be used to inform commuters that there is a transport interchange point or terminal close by at which they may change their mode of transport.' Artwork rendered and inspected: green rectangle, white border, with minibus, train, car and bus symbols and arrows converging on a central pedestrian — matching the same section's statement that 'a motorcar or mini-bus symbol represents informal transport, and a bus or train symbol formal transport'.

plainEnglish.en: A warning triangle with a yellow light that actually flashes. It is put on an already-bad spot to say this one is worse than the usual warning sign suggests.
plainEnglish.af: 'n Waarskuwingsdriehoek met 'n geel lig wat werklik flikker. Dit word by 'n reeds slegte plek gesit om te sê hierdie een is erger as wat die gewone waarskuwingsteken laat blyk.

formalMeaning.en: Warns of a hazard ahead by means of an intermittent flashing yellow light inside the warning triangle.
formalMeaning.af: Waarsku teen 'n gevaar vorentoe deur middel van 'n afwisselende flikkerende geel lig binne die waarskuwingsdriehoek.

behaviour.en: Slow down early and be ready to stop. It is normally mounted with another warning sign, so read that one for what the hazard actually is.
behaviour.af: Verminder spoed vroeg en wees gereed om te stop. Dit word gewoonlik saam met 'n ander waarskuwingsteken gemonteer, so lees daardie een vir wat die gevaar werklik is.

commonMistake.en: Taking the yellow disc for a traffic signal and waiting for it to change. It is a warning sign that flashes — it never turns green.
commonMistake.af: Om die geel skyf vir 'n verkeerslig aan te sien en te wag dat dit verander. Dit is 'n waarskuwingsteken wat flikker — dit word nooit groen nie.

testHint.en: A red triangle means warning, whatever sits inside it. The flashing yellow disc adds emphasis; it does not turn the sign into a signal.
testHint.af: 'n Rooi driehoek beteken waarskuwing, wat ook al binne dit is. Die flikkerende geel skyf gee klem; dit maak nie die teken 'n verkeerslig nie.

memoryTrick.en: Flashing yellow in a red triangle: extra bad, not a robot.
memoryTrick.af: Flikkerende geel in 'n rooi driehoek: ekstra sleg, nie 'n robot nie.

verification.reason: Chart match was already exact — code 'W346', name 'Emergency flashing light', p.2, score 1.0, and the chart index reads 'W346 Emergency flashing light sign'. The gap was content, not identity. SADC RTSM Vol 1 §3.4.37(1): 'The EMERGENCY FLASHING LIGHT warning sign W346 is to warn road users of a hazard ahead by means of an intermittent flashing yellow circular light within the warning sign.' §3.4.37(2) adds that its use 'should be to supplement some other warning sign to give it added emphasis'. Artwork rendered and inspected: red triangle, yellow circular disc, white background — matching the section's colour block field-for-field (Triangle: Red retroreflective / Symbol: Yellow flashing light / Background: White retroreflective).

content.note: AI-drafted lesson prose. Constraint 9 NOT satisfied — needs a human read. Teaching point chosen is that the flashing disc is not a signal, since a yellow light a learner can see flashing is the obvious thing to mistake for a robot. The 'supplements another warning sign' rule from §3.4.37(2) is carried into behaviour, because it tells the driver where to look for what the hazard actually is.
